title: Lattices after a finite stratification
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\cO_E$ and a uniformizer $\pi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. The standing schemes are separated schemes of finite type over the fixed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, $p\ne\ell$. The coefficients $E_X$ and $\cO_{E,X}$ are the pullbacks of the condensed topological rings $E$ and $\cO_E$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Modules mean module objects in abelian sheaves on the small pro-étale site [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Here lisse means locally free of finite rank for the pro-étale topology, with ranks allowed to vary; a lattice is a lisse $\cO_{E,X}$-submodule whose localization at $\ell$ is the given $E_X$-module. A finite stratification means a finite disjoint covering by locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification].

Statements with coefficients $\cO_E/\pi_E^n$ reach $E$-coefficients only through integral
lattices. A lisse $E_X$-module need not have a lattice on all of $X$, but it has one on each
stratum of a finite stratification, and for dévissage arguments this suffices. A global
lattice can fail to exist when $X$ is not normal. Let $X$ be a projective line with $0$ and
$\infty$ glued to a node, and let $Y\to X$ be the infinite chain of projective lines covering
it, an étale $\mathbf Z$-torsor. Descending $E_Y$ along $Y\to X$, with the generator of
$\mathbf Z$ acting by multiplication by $\ell$, gives a lisse $E_X$-module $L$ of rank one.
Since $Y$ is connected, a lattice in $L|_Y\cong E_Y$ is a constant lattice $\pi_E^m\cO_E$, and
no such lattice is stable under multiplication by $\ell$; so $L$ has no lattice on $X$. On the
open stratum $X\smallsetminus\{\text{node}\}\cong\mathbf G_m$ the torsor is trivial and $L$ is
constant.

Let $X$ be a standing scheme and $L$ a lisse $E_X$-module. There is a finite stratification
of $X$ by locally closed subschemes $S$ such that each $L|_S$ contains a lisse
$\cO_{E,S}$-submodule $L_0$ with $L_0[1/\ell]=L|_S$.

proof.text: A field is Noetherian because its only ideals are $0$ and the whole field. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian, and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes the standing $X$ Noetherian. Choose a finite affine cover with Noetherian coordinate rings. Each chart is topologically Noetherian by [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space]. An ascending chain of opens of $X$ stabilizes on each chart, hence on $X$ by taking the maximum of the finitely many stabilization indices. Thus $X$ is topologically Noetherian. Every open subset is quasi-compact: an open cover without a finite subcover would give a strictly increasing sequence of finite unions of its members. In particular $X$ and the intersections of any two affine opens are quasi-compact, so $X$ is qcqs. We may work with the continuous coefficient sheaves $U\mapsto C(|U|,\cO_E)$ and $U\mapsto C(|U|,E)$: [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-realizations] identifies them with the pulled condensed coefficients, compatibly with the inclusion $\cO_E\to E$. Its total-disconnectedness hypothesis holds: distinct points of an ultrametric field are separated by disjoint clopen balls; the valuation ring inherits this property. Module-object actions are precisely the sectionwise module laws, so these ring isomorphisms transport the modules and their inclusions. By [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-invert-ell], the integral-to-rational coefficient map is localization at $\ell$. These identifications will also be used on every scheme appearing below.

source.place: Definition 6.8.1 and Lemma 6.8.2; continuous realization comparison and the standing finite-type hypothesis

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-etale-local-lattice] to $L$, regarded through step 1 as an internal continuous rational module. It gives a qcqs scheme $V$, an étale surjection $p:V\to X$, a pro-étale locally finite free integral module $M_0$ on $V$, and an isomorphism $M_0[1/\ell]\simeq p^*L$. The natural map $M_0\to M_0[1/\ell]$ is injective: on a trivializing cover it is a finite direct sum of the injective inclusion $C(-,\cO_E)\to C(-,E)$. Compose with the displayed isomorphism to regard $M_0$ as a lattice submodule of $p^*L$. This is the sheaf-of-lattices and finite-cover part of the blueprint: the cited theorem already allows varying finite ranks and supplies the quasi-compact cover, so no reduction to a globally constant rank is needed.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(6) and the initial finite-cover reduction of Lemma 6.8.13

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-stratified-finite] to $p:V\to X$, whose source and target are qcqs. Obtain finitely many constructible locally closed subschemes $S_a\to X$ partitioning $X$ and finite étale morphisms $p_a:V\times_X S_a\to S_a$. Every $p_a$ is surjective: for a point of $S_a$ a point in the nonempty fibre of $p$ remains after the residue-field extension defining that fibre product. The locally free modules and their rationalization isomorphisms pull back to these schemes by [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-locally-free-pullback]; the coefficient identifications of step 1 intertwine the integral-to-rational maps. Explicitly, on a chart with integral basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$, scalar extension has rational basis $1\otimes e_1,\ldots,1\otimes e_r$. Inverse image pulls these bases back to bases for the corresponding coefficient rings on the base-changed chart. The matrix of the given rationalization isomorphism and the matrix of its inverse pull back to inverse matrices, since pullback preserves their two product identities. Thus the pulled-back scalar-extension map is the rationalization isomorphism on these charts; the maps agree on overlaps because they are induced by the original map. The integral inclusion is injective in these bases, so the pulled-back $M_0$ remains a lattice. Fix one nonempty $S=S_a$ and write $p:V_S\to S$, $M=M_0|_{V_S}$ and $L_S=L|_S$.

source.place: Tag 03S0 (etale-cohomology-lemma-etale-stratified-finite); blueprint proof, Pushing down by the trace

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-etale-local-split], $S$ has an étale covering on which $V_S$ is a finite disjoint union of copies of the base. On a splitting with sheets indexed by a finite set $J$, define $\operatorname{Tr}:p_*p^*L_S\to L_S$ by $(s_j)_{j\in J}\mapsto\sum_js_j$. Two splittings, after a common étale refinement, differ by a permutation of the sheets on clopen pieces. Finite sums are invariant under these permutations, so the maps agree on overlaps and glue by the sheaf axiom. This constructs an $E_S$-linear trace on the pro-étale site itself. Define $L_0\subseteq L_S$ to consist of sections which locally are traces of sections of $p_*M$. This is an $\cO_{E,S}$-submodule sheaf: local expressions remain such on restriction and glue locally; after a common refinement, sums of trace expressions and their integral scalar multiples are traces of the corresponding sums and multiples of sections of $p_*M$. On a splitting write $M_j\subseteq L_S$ for its restrictions to the sheets; the definition then gives $L_0=\sum_{j\in J}M_j$. Surjectivity of $p$ implies $J\ne\varnothing$ over any nonempty splitting neighbourhood.

source.place: Pushing down by the trace, definition of the trace and its local sum description (splitting: Stacks Tag 04HN)

proof.text: Refine a splitting neighbourhood pro-étale locally to make $L_S\simeq E_S^r$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lattice-sheaf-locally-constant], each embedded lattice $M_j\subseteq E_S^r$ is represented by a section of the constant sheaf on $\operatorname{GL}_r(E)/\operatorname{GL}_r(\cO_E)$. A section of a constant sheaf is locally the image of an element of that set. Since $J$ is finite, successively refining these finitely many covers gives a common pro-étale refinement on which every $M_j$ is the continuous coefficient module of a fixed lattice $\Lambda_j\subseteq E^r$. Thus the remaining question concerns the finite sum $\Lambda=\sum_{j\in J}\Lambda_j$ inside $E^r$. This uses the full classification assertion of the cited node, rather than a representability assertion with a missing classification clause.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(6), identification of the lattice sheaf with the discrete lattice-coset sheaf; blueprint trace paragraph

proof.text: The union of finite bases of the $\Lambda_j$ generates $\Lambda$ over $\cO_E$. As a submodule of $E^r$, $\Lambda$ is torsion-free. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $\cO_E$ is a DVR with fraction field $E$, so [lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free] makes $\Lambda$ finite free. Because $J\ne\varnothing$, $\Lambda$ contains a lattice $\Lambda_j$ spanning $E^r$; its localization at $\ell$ is therefore $E^r$, and its free rank is $r$. Give $\Lambda$ and every $\Lambda_j$ their subspace topologies in $E^r$. The chosen $\cO_E$-basis of $\Lambda$ is an $E$-basis of $E^r$, since $\Lambda[1/\ell]=E^r$. Its basis matrix and inverse over $E$ define continuous inverse maps on $E^r$ (each coordinate is a finite sum of scalar products). Restricting them identifies $\cO_E^r$ homeomorphically with $\Lambda$. The same argument applies to each $\Lambda_j$. Moreover the sheaf sum of the continuous modules of the $\Lambda_j$ equals the continuous module of $\Lambda$. Indeed $\bigoplus_j\Lambda_j\to\Lambda$ is a surjective linear map and has a linear section: choose a basis of the free module $\Lambda$ and a preimage of each basis vector. In chosen finite bases this section is a matrix over $\cO_E$, hence is continuous. Applying continuous functions on any site object therefore preserves this surjection and its section. This verifies the trace-image computation at the level of sheaves, not just at individual fibres.

source.place: Pushing down by the trace, finite sum of lattices; algebraic freeness: Stacks Tag 0AUW (more-algebra-lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat), part (3)

proof.text: On the common covering of steps 5 and 6, $L_0$ is consequently isomorphic to $\cO_{E,S}^r$, and its inclusion into $L_S$ becomes an isomorphism after inverting $\ell$. Both conclusions are local: the first is exactly the definition of lisse, while the localization maps glue because each is induced by the one inclusion $L_0\subseteq L_S$. An isomorphism can be checked on a cover, since its local inverses agree on overlaps and hence glue. This supplies a lisse lattice on every nonempty $S_a$; discard empty strata. If $X$ is empty take the empty stratification, and if a local rank is zero take the zero lattice. The finitely many $S_a$ are the required stratification.
